CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation for potential kidney abnormalities associated with Smith-Magenis Syndrome.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 22-month-old former 34 and 3-week-old gestational age twin female with Smith-Magenis Syndrome presenting for nephrology evaluation. She was born weighing 4 pounds 8 ounces. As a newborn, she had difficulty with feeding-related apnea and temperature regulation, typical of prematurity. She was initially exclusively on cow's milk but was transitioned to ripple pea protein milk due to poor tolerance. She has severe gastroesophageal reflux and follows with a gastroenterologist and dietician. She has been diagnosed with Smith-Magenis Syndrome by neurology due to developmental delay, specifically not walking or sitting independently at one year of age. She is now crawling and attempting to take steps. She is engaged in multiple therapies including feeding therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, and will be starting speech therapy within the next couple weeks. She has also been evaluated by orthopedics, ophthalmology, and audiology. Regarding voiding, mother reports approximately 8-10 wet diapers per 24-hour period. Fluid intake has improved since discontinuing dairy milk, with patient now drinking pea protein milk and water with occasional dilute juice. Mother notes patient drinks and urinates frequently.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for history of feeding difficulties with apnea, poor temperature regulation as a newborn, severe gastroesophageal reflux, and developmental delay. Negative for dysuria, hematuria, or edema. Twin sister is healthy and developmentally normal, weighing approximately the same as patient.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Smith-Magenis Syndrome (chromosomal deletion syndrome), prematurity (34 weeks 3 days gestation), history of feeding-related apnea, gastroesophageal reflux disease, failure to thrive/feeding intolerance with cow's milk, developmental delay.

MEDICATIONS
Not documented in visit.

ALLERGIES
Not documented in visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sibling (9-year-old son) with autism. No family history of kidney failure, dialysis, or renal transplant.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient lives in Dallas, Georgia with family including mother (present at visit), father, twin sister, and 9-year-old brother. Attends multiple therapy sessions.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-nourished female, slightly fussy during examination.
HEENT: Eyes small-appearing.
Neurologic: Mild hypotonia of lower extremities and arms.
Genitourinary: Normal external female genitalia.
Cardiovascular and Pulmonary: Normal to auscultation (listened to heart and lungs).

RESULTS
Pending kidney ultrasound.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
22-month-old former 34 weeks 3-day-old twin female with Smith-Magenis Syndrome. Smith-Magenis Syndrome is a chromosomal deletion syndrome that can affect multiple organ systems. Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) have been reported in association with this syndrome. Plan to screen for kidney abnormalities with renal ultrasound today. If abnormalities are found, further workup and management will be determined. If ultrasound is normal, no further follow-up needed. Results will be communicated to family. Patient will follow up at Town Center location given family residence in Dallas, Georgia. Family instructed to complete paperwork and provided instructions for ultrasound procedure.
